title: From Right to Oblique Triangles Practice
description: Practice identifying right and oblique triangles and naming triangle-solving given cases.

questions.question: Which triangle is an oblique triangle?
options: A triangle with one angle equal to 180 degrees
A triangle that must have three equal sides
questions.explanation: An oblique triangle is any triangle with no right angle.

questions.question: A triangle has angles 30 degrees, 60 degrees, and 90 degrees. How should it be classified first?
questions.explanation: The 90-degree angle makes it a right triangle. The given-case labels are used after noticing the triangle type.

questions.question: A triangle has angles 42 degrees, 63 degrees, and 75 degrees. How should it be classified?
questions.explanation: There is no 90-degree angle, so the triangle is oblique. All three angles are less than 90 degrees, so it is acute.

questions.question: A triangle has angles 25 degrees, 35 degrees, and 120 degrees. How should it be classified?
questions.explanation: The triangle has no 90-degree angle, so it is oblique. The 120-degree angle makes it obtuse.

questions.question: You know two angles of a triangle and the side between those two angles. Which case is this?
questions.explanation: Two known angles with the included side form the ASA case.

questions.question: You know two angles and a side that is not between the two known angles. Which case is this?
questions.explanation: Two angles and a non-included side form the AAS case.

questions.question: You know two side lengths and the angle between those side lengths. Which case is this?
questions.explanation: Two sides with their included angle form the SAS case.

questions.question: You know all three side lengths of a triangle. Which case is this?
questions.explanation: Three known side lengths form the SSS case.

questions.question: SSA means two sides and a non-included angle are known.
questions.explanation: SSA has two known sides and an angle that is not between those sides.

questions.question: Write the three-letter case for this information: two sides and the included angle.
questions.explanation: Two sides and the included angle are named in order as Side-Angle-Side, or SAS.
